messages:
olivia (support): Heads-up — customer AcmeAI reporting large tail-latency spikes on the embeddings route since ~17:01 UTC. p99 jumping from ~120ms to ~2.1s for ~30s windows. They’re seeing a lot of 503s/502s too.

mohit (eng-runtime): Can you paste one of the request samples + any shard logs? suspect dynbatch behavior or a corner-case with max_batch_size.

olivia (support): Pasting sanitized excerpt from their payloads and the runtime log around the spike. Note: they send mixed small (1-5 vectors) and huge (1024 vectors).

olivia (support): ```
# client snippet (sanitized)
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "embed-xlarge-4096",
  "input": [[...], ...]  # mixture of 1-5 and 1024-length items
}

# runtime log stream (abridged)
[17:01:12] batcher: coalesce_window_us=8000 max_batch_size=64 current_slots=64 filled_by_req_id=af1a
[17:01:12] shard-7: dispatched kernel seq_len=4096 slots=64 est_tokens=258k
[17:01:12] client-proxy: 502 response to request id=bf3c (timeout downstream)
[17:01:13] batcher: backpressure applied, small-requests queued=123
[17:01:14] shard-7: finish, flush took 1.9s
```

mohit (eng-runtime): Interesting — looks like a large request consumed an entire max_batch_size window and the flush cost (large seq_len) caused subsequent small requests to pile up. That explains p99 spike. Any signs of client retries during the window? retries can multiply queue pressure.

olivia (support): They had an exponential-retry policy on 5xx with no jitter for 500/502. Logs show ~3 immediate retries from same token during the 17:01-17:02 window.

sarah (eng-sre): ops-bot shows ingress rate spike ~+40% coincident with the timeline. I can see token-based concurrency limits were hit for that customer.

ops-bot: ALERT: token=acct-acmeai exceeded per-token concurrency 32 -> throttling applied at 17:01:13

mohit (eng-runtime): Repro plan: simulate mixed-size stream with a single client token, no retry jitter, max_batch_size=64, coalesce_ms=8. Should see starvation of small reqs and p99 spike when a heavy request hits. Here's a repro script sketch:```python
# pseudo
for t in range(100):
  if t % 20 == 0:
    send_large_request(n_vectors=1024)
  else:
    send_small_request(n_vectors=random.randint(1,5))
  time.sleep(0.01)
```

mohit (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigations:
- Ask customer to enable jitter on retries (recommended).
- Create separate route/API key for bulk upload traffic so it doesn’t share batching pool with low-latency single-vector calls.
- Reduce max_batch_size for the embeddings route (e.g., 64 -> 32) or enable slot-partitioning so huge requests don’t claim all slots.

olivia (support): I already told them to add jitter + backoff and to avoid retrying on 502s immediately. They asked if we can change routing from our side.

sarah (eng-sre): I can apply a temporary route override for AcmeAI: set route.max_batch_size=32 and enable small_request_priority=true for 30m window to see if tail fixes. Will also enable tighter ingress token throttling (burst tokens=8).

mohit (eng-runtime): Longer term: we should add preemption to the coalescer — allow small priority requests to preempt unstarted slots, and consider max_slots_per_request to cap very large client bundles (e.g., max_client_request_slots=16). Also audit our default retry guidance in docs.

olivia (support): I'll send the customer the temporary change offer and ask them to enable jitter. Also opened a support escalation with Acct team.

ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2345 — Embedding-batcher starvation by mixed-size bursts (assigned: eng-runtime, eng-sre).

mohit (eng-runtime): For the investigation note — check batcher metrics: slots_claimed_by_request, avg_flush_tokens, flush_duration_ms, and request_retry_count per token. Also correlate with kernel dispatch durations.

sarah (eng-sre): I captured flamegraphs for that 17:01 dispatch. flush duration dominated by attention kernel at high seq len (expected). But we can reduce observable p99 by either limiting slots per request or breaking large client bundles before kernel dispatch.

olivia (support): Customer responded: they can gate large bulk jobs to off-hours if we prefer, and will split big uploads. Meanwhile accepting our temporary route change. Thanks team, will update once customer confirms. :thumbsup:
